C3.label: refuted
C3.text: Fewer than half of enterprise generative-AI pilots generally deliver no measurable return.

C4.label: untested
C4.reason: no evidence bears on the claim and no argument tests it
C4.text: Enterprise generative-AI pilots have no general tendency to fail to deliver measurable returns.

C5.label: accepted
C5.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C5.text: “No measurable return” conflates unmeasured benefits, absent financial impact, and negative returns; these interpretations yield different answers about enterprise generative-AI pilots.

C6.label: contested
C6.reason: standing pro and con arguments prevent an accepted answer
C6.text: MIT NANDA's 2025 State of AI in Business report originated the widely circulated claim that 95% of organizations were getting zero return from generative-AI investments.

C8.label: unsupported
C8.reason: evidence bears on the claim but no supporting argument was built
C8.text: No identifiable research report originated the roughly 95% claim about enterprise generative-AI pilots.

C9.label: contested
C9.reason: standing pro and con arguments prevent an accepted answer
C9.text: The originating material shifts between organizations, investments, and pilots, so its roughly 95% statements do not identify a single consistent denominator.

C10.label: accepted
C10.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C10.text: The originating research studied a selected set of enterprise AI initiatives using interviews, surveys, and public cases, rather than a probability sample of enterprise generative-AI pilots.

C11.label: accepted
C11.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C11.text: The originating research assessed enterprise generative-AI returns through reported organizational outcomes, rather than audited financial returns for every sampled pilot.

C13.label: refuted
C13.text: The originating research did not assess returns from enterprise generative-AI projects.

C15.label: refuted
C15.text: Google Cloud's 2024 survey reported that 74% of organizations using generative AI in production saw ROI on at least one use case; this was not a pilot-level return rate.

C17.label: unsupported
C17.reason: evidence bears on the claim but no supporting argument was built
C17.text: Other empirical studies report no proportions or outcome distributions concerning returns from enterprise generative-AI projects.

C18.label: accepted
C18.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C18.text: Other studies report organization-level, production-use, or broader AI outcomes rather than comparable enterprise generative-AI pilot return rates.

C19.label: accepted
C19.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C19.text: NANDA reports zero return for 95% of organizations; separately, it says 5% of integrated AI pilots extract millions and the vast majority have no measurable P&L impact.

C20.label: accepted
C20.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C20.text: NANDA reports that 60% of organizations evaluated enterprise-grade tools, 20% reached pilots and 5% reached production; these are adoption-stage shares, not pilot return rates.

C21.label: accepted
C21.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C21.text: The complement of the reported 5% of integrated pilots extracting millions is 95% not meeting that threshold, not 95% demonstrated to lack any measurable benefit.

C22.label: contested
C22.reason: standing pro and con arguments prevent an accepted answer
C22.text: NANDA's report says 5% of integrated AI pilots extract millions in value, while the vast majority have no measurable P&L impact.

C23.label: accepted
C23.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C23.text: The report states that ROI impact was measured six months post-pilot and adjusted for department size; the supplied methodology passages do not identify the pilot denominator or calculation behind the headline proportion.

C25.label: refuted
C25.text: The supplied NANDA report does not establish that roughly 95% of enterprise generative-AI pilots generally deliver no measurable return: its headline pilot denominator is unidentified, and its statement about no measurable P&L impact does not demonstrate an absence of all benefits.

C26.label: refuted
C26.text: The report separates evaluation, pilot and production stages, reports different implementation timelines across firm categories, and warns that six months may be insufficient for complex enterprise deployments; the supplied passages do not establish how timing or implementation maturity affected the headline return proportion.

C27.label: refuted
C27.text: The supplied secondary article attributes to IBM's 2025 CEO study a finding that 25% of AI initiatives had delivered expected ROI; it does not identify these as exclusively enterprise generative-AI pilots or reproduce the primary study's design and uncertainty.
